summary: Advisory source review only; I executed nothing. This is not native controller approval, human review, final QA or release authority. The three prior Max findings appear addressed in source: TLS key disposal now starts synchronously, session cleanup owns pending startup, and the staging, claim and transition paths keep their classification when close rejects. Three confirmed defects in cleanup and receipt truthfulness remain. (1) A startup rejection is always reported as cleanup failure, even when the runtime factory has already completed its cleanup. (2) A cleanup failure during release is reported as a provider or validation failure, with no cleanupFailed evidence, and it discards an otherwise valid report after the round has been spent. (3) A cleanup failure during native qualification is lost from the capability-blocked receipt. I found no path that weakens one-forward, request, response or claim fencing: close fails the state synchronously, and the forward wrapper keeps its policy, liveness and deadline checks. I also found no unbounded await on the reviewed session paths, and removal targets only the observed container ID. Local and hosted test results are supplied evidence only, not live Docker or guarded native qualification.

findings.problem: Confirmed from source. Session cleanup runs `runtime ?? (await startup)`, so any startup rejection makes boundedCleanup report native-session-cleanup-failed. createNativeRuntimeFactory throws native-runtime-rejected only after its own `await cleanup()` has succeeded, meaning owned resources were already stopped and the private directory removed. A failure in certificate creation, proxy listen or mount validation therefore becomes a false cleanup failure, because the catch block's `await close()` rejects before native-session-rejected can be thrown. The worker then sets cleanupFailed: true and returns queue-blocked early (cloud-review-worker.mjs, staging catch), which also stops later queue candidates that the clean path would still try. Proven-clean and unknown outcomes are not distinguishable, contrary to AC2 of the first task contract and step 4 of its plan.
findings.requested_change: Have session cleanup recognize a trusted factory signal that cleanup was already proven, and treat that startup rejection as nothing left to close. Prefer a private WeakSet-minted error, like the existing capacity classification, over matching free text. Keep native-session-cleanup-failed for a factory cleanup failure, an unrecognized startup rejection, a hung startup and any late close failure. The caller should then receive native-session-rejected on the proven-clean path.
findings.test_expectation: Add real child or session tests for three cases. A startup rejecting with the trusted proven-clean signal yields native-session-rejected, zero forwards and no cleanupFailed in the worker, and a later candidate is still processed. A factory whose cleanup fails, and an unknown startup rejection, both yield native-session-cleanup-failed. A factory-level test should show the directory removed on the proven-clean path and retained on the failed path.

findings.problem: Confirmed from source. The `finally { await close(); }` in session.release replaces a fully validated result with native-session-cleanup-failed when cleanup is unproven. The worker's bare catch at this line cannot see that cause. It calls failOwnedClaim with the default review-validation-failed code, keeps the runner-threw diagnostic, and returns provider-failed with no cleanupFailed field. The same omission applies if failOwnedClaim then reports ownership-changed. A real forward that returned a genuine verified report is therefore recorded as a provider or validation failure, the report is lost, the round is spent, and the possibly live container or retained directory leaves no receipt signal. The r2 change added cleanupFailed to staging, claim and transition only, while this post-reservation path is where the stricter container proof matters most.
findings.requested_change: Bind the error in this catch and add sanitized cleanupFailed: true to the provider-failed and ownership-changed receipts when the cause is native-session-cleanup-failed. Do not retry, refund or forward again. Do not report the failure as a report-validation defect; if the controller's failure codes allow it, record a distinct code, otherwise retain the existing code and add explicit evidence. Separately decide, and document, whether a fully validated report should be retained as hash-bound evidence alongside the cleanup failure rather than discarded.
findings.test_expectation: Add processCloudReview tests where release rejects with native-session-cleanup-failed. Assert exactly one release and one failOwnedClaim, no second claim or inference, a nonzero-exit status, cleanupFailed: true, and no private text in the receipt. Repeat with failOwnedClaim throwing review-ownership-changed. Add a stageGuardedSession test confirming that the chosen report-retention behavior holds when forwarding succeeds and close fails.

findings.problem: Confirmed from source. In native-review mode, the probe runs qualifyNativeGuardOnHost, which starts a real guarded container for the synthetic forward. If stage or release fails with native-session-cleanup-failed, qualifyNativeGuard's catch rethrows a generic rejection (native-guard-qualification.mjs). This worker catch then discards the error entirely and returns capability-blocked without cleanupFailed. A container or directory whose removal is unproven is thus indistinguishable from an ordinary qualification failure, even though the staging and claim paths now report that evidence. The qualify-native mode ends in the conservative worker-failed unknown receipt, but it too carries no cleanup signal.
findings.requested_change: Preserve a sanitized cleanup-failure classification through qualifyNativeGuard without exposing any other error detail, and add cleanupFailed: true to the capability-blocked receipt when it applies. Keep the outcome nonqualified and nonretryable. Emit the same field from the qualify-native CLI failure path if that path can carry it safely.
findings.test_expectation: Inject a qualification source or session whose close rejects with native-session-cleanup-failed. Assert that the result is rejected, that processCloudReview returns capability-blocked with cleanupFailed: true, claimed: false, no claim call and no release of application source, and that no private text is present. An ordinary qualification failure must not set the field.

limitations: Static source review only: I ran no tools, tests, Docker, provider or model. Line numbers were derived by manual counting from diff hunks and should be confirmed against the file.

Live Docker behavior is unproven. Hypothesis, not reproduced: rm --force colliding with an in-progress auto-removal could give a nonzero rm with a still-visible ID, producing a fail-closed cleanup-unproven result with no bounded re-check.

Confirmed by reading, not treated as a defect: if docker run exits or inspection fails before an ID is observed, close reports cleanup-unproven and retains the private directory even when no container was created. This is conservative, but its live frequency is unknown.

Container cleanup can take several consecutive windows (ID wait, rm, list) while the outer bound is one window, so an outer failure can precede a later successful removal. This is conservative and not reported as a defect.

comment-review-handoff.mjs, standalone-review.mjs, cloud-review-recovery-worker.mjs and their controllers were not supplied. Allowed failure codes, failOwnedClaim behavior and recovery receipts were therefore not assessed.
The exact failure site of run 41937588247 and its inference outcome remain unknown; this source cannot resolve them.

Supplied evidence is not treated as proof of real behavior: local results on Windows CLI 2.1.296, 3 Linux-specific skips, mocked Docker, partial hosted CI still in progress at preparation, no guarded Docker or Max qualification on Linux pinned CLI 2.1.301, and no one-forward or request-cap proof from a lower observed output count.

Independent native human approval, a native subject or claim, post-review QA, candidate deployment and parity are all absent. This advisory authorizes no merge, deployment, retry, refund or allowance change.
